column1: # WADI: higher score = more vulnerable to AI/automation displacement
# Average % of female workforce in high-risk sectors: 48.9%
# Bangladesh: 4M women garment workers face near-total automation by 2030
# Japan: 75% of at-risk admin jobs held by women
# Philippines: 1.3M women in call centres — 79% automation risk
# India: 230M+ women in high-risk jobs across sectors

column15: notes
MOST EXPOSED: 90% of garment workers are women. H&M, Zara factories automating. 700,000 jobs at risk by 2030. Entire female economy depends on one high-risk sector.
CRITICAL: 4M women garment workers — highest global automation risk. 80% of export garment workforce is female. Automation of sewing = 4M job losses projected by 2030. No reskilling infrastructure.
Hawassa Industrial Park: 60,000 women garment workers. Chinese-owned factories automating fastest. Zero reskilling.
Textile sector (70% female) — automation of spinning, weaving. Low digital literacy. No AI gender policy.
Market trader women — platform competition from Jumia/Konga. Fintech disrupting women's savings cooperatives (ajo/esusu).
Batik, garment, tobacco processing — all high automation risk. Ojek (ride-share) gig workers — women excluded by safety concerns.
2.8M women in electronics/garment assembly. Samsung, Nike automation. Digital economy growing but women capture only 12% of tech jobs.
Market women — platform competition. Cocoa processing automation.

230M women in high-risk jobs: garment (8M), data entry (12M), domestic work (30M+). Digital skills gap severe. Only 3% female AI workforce. BPO sector (call centres) employs 2M women — 70% automation risk.
Tea plucking (women) — robotisation beginning. Garment sector.
M-Pesa disrupted women money handlers. Flower export sector at risk. Growing digital economy but women capture small share.
1.3M women in BPO (call centres) — 75% female, 79% automation risk. Remittance-dependent economy: OFW (overseas workers) also exposed.
Government digital inclusion programs for women. Tech hub growing.
Maquiladora sector (export manufacturing) — 60% female, high automation. NAFTA reshoring + AI = double pressure. No federal retraining.
Domestic work (1.4M women) — no labour protections. Mining sector automation minimal female impact (few women in mining).
Textile sector (85% female) — highest automation risk in manufacturing.
Domestic workers (5.7M women) — informal, no safety net. Afro-Brazilian women most exposed. Gig platform workers unprotected.
Foxconn automation displacing 1M+ women. Wenzhou shoe factories. Strong government retraining programs but rural women excluded.
75% of at-risk admin jobs held by women. Lowest AI/tech female participation. 'Shufu' system traps women in part-time.
High export manufacturing exposure. Women concentrated in textiles.
No federal reskilling mandate. Garment, admin, call centre exposure high. Gig economy vulnerable.
2.4M women in admin at risk. Universal Credit inadequate. Taylor Review gaps.
Strong protections but 1.8M women in high-risk roles.
Manufacturing automation. 4 million women in admin jobs at risk. Kurzarbeit protects.
Strong reskilling programs. Indigenous women most exposed.
Automation commission includes gender. High digital literacy.
Oil sector automation displacing women in admin. Strong retraining programs.
Strong social protection. AI strategy includes gender clause. Low garment sector.
